# Turn a voice memo into a polished meeting summary with Hugging Face’s free speech-to-text

> **In short:** Hugging Face hosts a free web demo of OpenAI's Whisper speech-recognition model. You upload a recording or use your microphone, click Submit, and get the spoken words as text. Then you clean up the text and shape it into a summary.

You've just recorded a quick voice memo: a brainstorm, a call recap, or a team update. Typing it out takes time. With the Whisper demo on Hugging Face, you can get a text version in a few minutes, then turn it into a summary you can send.

## Before you start

- **A voice recording** saved as an audio file on your phone or computer, or a microphone to record directly.
- **A web browser.** If the demo asks you to sign in, you can create a free Hugging Face account.
- **Permission to record.** If other people's voices are in the memo, make sure they know and agree.
- **About 5–10 minutes.**

## Step 1: Prepare your recording

Play your memo once to check that it is clear and complete. If your recording app can trim clips, cut long silences at the start and end. Save it as a common audio file type, such as MP3 or WAV.

💬 Example: Save your memo as `team-update.mp3`.

You'll know it worked when you have one clear audio file ready to upload.

## Step 2: Open the Whisper demo on Hugging Face

Go to [huggingface.co/spaces/openai/whisper](https://huggingface.co/spaces/openai/whisper). This Space is titled "Whisper Large V3: Transcribe Audio." Hugging Face Spaces are small web apps that people and companies publish so you can try AI models in your browser.

You'll know it worked when you see the demo page with an audio area, a **Task** choice, and a **Submit** button. The app may take a moment to start if it hasn't been used recently.

## Step 3: Add your audio and choose the task

In the audio area, upload your file or record with your microphone. Under **Task**, keep **transcribe** to get the text in the language that was spoken. Choose **translate** only if you want the text translated into English.

You'll know it worked when your audio appears in the audio area and you can play it back.

## Step 4: Click Submit and wait for the text

Click **Submit**. The text appears in the output box when it's done. Longer recordings take longer, and the wait can also depend on how busy the demo is. If you see an error, try again a little later or with a shorter clip.

You'll know it worked when the output box shows the words from your recording.

## Step 5: Copy the text and fix mistakes

Copy the text from the output box and paste it into a document or note. Read it while you listen to the memo again. Speech recognition can mishear names, numbers, and technical terms, so correct those first.

💬 Example: Change "the launch is on June fifth" to "the launch is on June 5" if that is what was meant.

You'll know it worked when the text matches what was said.

## Step 6: Turn it into a summary

Now shape the text into a short summary. You can do it yourself with headings like **Key points**, **Decisions**, and **Next steps**, or paste the corrected text into an AI chat assistant you already use and ask for a summary. Check the summary against your transcript before you share it.

💬 Example: "Turn this transcript into a short meeting summary with three sections: key points, decisions, and next steps with the person responsible: [paste your corrected transcript]"

You'll know it worked when you have a short, accurate summary ready to share.

## Common mistakes

- **A noisy or very long recording.** Background noise makes mistakes more likely, and long files take longer. *The fix:* Record in a quiet place and try a short clip first.
- **Choosing "translate" by accident.** That option gives you English text. *The fix:* Keep **transcribe** if you want the original language.
- **Sharing the raw text.** The transcript can contain misheard words. *The fix:* Correct names, dates, and numbers before you summarize or share.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Turn a spoken to-do list or a voice note into text you can search and edit.
- **For your business or work:** Get a written record of a short internal update, then send a checked summary to your team. Don't upload confidential recordings to a public demo.
- **If you're just getting started:** Start with a 30-second memo to see how the demo works before you try longer files.

## Try it now

Record a 30-second voice memo about your plans for tomorrow. Open [huggingface.co/spaces/openai/whisper](https://huggingface.co/spaces/openai/whisper), upload the memo, keep **transcribe**, and click **Submit**. Then copy the text and fix any misheard words.
